cards.front: What should you know about concentration?
cards.back: The amount of solute dissolved in a given volume of solution. Measured in g/dm³ or mol/dm³.

cards.front: What should you know about percentage yield?
cards.back: The percentage of the theoretical maximum amount of product actually obtained from a reaction.

cards.front: What should you know about atom economy?
cards.back: The percentage of atoms in the reactants that end up in the desired product. A measure of how efficiently atoms are used.

cards.front: What should you know about why actual yield is always less than theoretical?
cards.back: Incomplete reactions: Not all reactants are converted to products Product lost: Some product is lost during separation and purification (e.g. left on filter paper) Reversible reactions: Some products react back to form reactants Side reactions: Unexpected reactions produce unwanted by-products
Concentration: Concentration (g/dm³) = mass (g) ÷ volume (dm³). Convert cm³ to dm³ by dividing by 1000. For mol/dm³: concentration = moles ÷ volume (dm³).

High yield means high atom economy. Wrong: high yield = high atom economy Correct: they measure different things — yield measures practical efficiency (how much you actually make), atom economy measures how efficiently atoms are used (how much waste is produced)
